# SRA cautions profession about safe and responsible use of AI in legal sector

17 August 2026

Amid growing day-to-day use in law firms, the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) has published a warning notice to remind the legal profession of their professional obligations when using AI (artificial intelligence). [...] The SRA received 42 reports related to the potential misuse of AI between July 2025 and July 2026. There are a number of ongoing investigations relating to misuse of AI, including on issues relating to inaccurate legal citations, supervision and confidentiality. The SRA added further sections to its guidance on effective supervision relating to AI in June this year. [...] The SRA will continue to work with the profession and other stakeholders to promote safe and responsible use of AI. As part of its proposed business plan for 2026/27, the SRA plans to strengthen its Innovate work programme to provide clear, practical, and policy-led support for firms looking to innovate and adopt technology.

# SRA sounds alarm on AI misuse

17 Aug 2026

1 minute read

## News

In the wake of the increased use of technology in the legal profession, the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) has today (17 August 2026) published a warning notice on the misuse of AI, advising how solicitors can responsibly use new technology in their practice. [...] The warning notice outlines the need for solicitors to check the information put before the courts, supervise the work undertaken for clients, and remain accountable for everything produced using AI.

As AI develops fast, the legal profession will continue to need timely and clear guidance on how to respond to emerging technologies.

Law Society of England and Wales vice president, Brett Dixon, said: [...] “The Law Society recognises that AI should be used to support and enhance legal practice, not to replace the essential role of solicitors in providing trusted advice to clients.

"We welcome the SRA’s warning notice and the clarity the guidance provides around how the use of AI interacts with the provision of legal services by solicitors, particularly in relation to the courts and the protection of client confidentiality.

Warning notice

# Misuse of AI

Published: 17 August 2026

Print this pageSave as PDF [...] This warning notice is relevant to all firms and individuals we regulate. It relates to the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the provision of legal services by regulated firms and individuals. While it is directed at those we regulate, it is also likely to be relevant to other authorised persons practising within SRA-regulated firms.

## What is AI and what is gen AI? [...] This Warning Notice focuses on the risks and issues relating to AI that have come to our attention. We recognise that many firms and legal professionals are already taking a considered, risk-based approach to the use of AI.

As the use of AI continues to evolve, we will continue to engage with the profession, monitor developments and share information to help those we regulate understand how their existing professional obligations apply when using AI.
